card.name: Frequency words after statistics
card.fires_on: Time-frequency words such as every, day, month, year, annually or daily that end a statistic about how often something happens, in general web text.

modes.label: Unit after every/each
modes.description: The time unit (day, month, year) right after every, each or a.
modes.example: Americans consume 721 bottles and cans of drinks per person every<< year>>, for an average of two per day

modes.label: Every or adverb itself
modes.description: The word every, or an adverb like annually or daily, closing a rate in a statistic.
modes.example: Nearly 8 million Americans go to work<< every>> day yet still live below the poverty line

card.plain: It marks the point where a statistic says how often something happens, such as every year or each month.
evidence: Nearly 8 million Americans go to work<< every>> day yet still live below the poverty line
On average, Facebook users create 90 pieces of content every<< month>> (Facebook 2011).
It is estimated that around 8,000 swan rescues take place each<< year>>.
